summary:
⚠️ Risk Score: MEDIUM (45/100)

1 Critical · 1 High · 1 Medium

Review completed with 3 findings across 2 agents (1 critical, 1 high, 1 medium).

⚠️ 2 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [CRITICAL] Reintroduction of XSS via URLField in Django Admin (SecurityAgent)
  - [HIGH] Removal of security regression test (SecurityAgent)

findings.title: Reintroduction of XSS via URLField in Django Admin
findings.description: This diff removes the URLValidator check that was added to mitigate CVE-2026-15920. Without this validation, stored values in URLField with dangerous schemes (javascript:, data:) will be rendered as clickable links in the admin interface. An attacker who can store such a value (e.g., via a form submission or direct database access) can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of any admin user who views the changelist or read-only field.

findings.title: Removal of security regression test
findings.description: The test `test_url_display_for_field_invalid_url` was removed. This test specifically verified that dangerous URL schemes (javascript:, data:) are not rendered as clickable links. Removing this test eliminates the safety net that would catch reintroduction of the vulnerability.
findings.suggestion:
Restore the test case to ensure the XSS vulnerability remains fixed:

```python
def test_url_display_for_field_invalid_url(self):
    model_field = models.URLField()
    for value in [
        "javascript:alert(1)",
        "data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>",
    ]:
        with self.subTest(value=value):
            display_value = display_for_field(value, model_field, self.empty_value)
            self.assertNotIn("<a", display_value)
            self.assertEqual(display_value, value)
```

findings.title: Removal of security advisory documentation
findings.description: The CVE-2026-15920 security advisory entries were removed from both docs/releases/5.2.17.txt and docs/releases/6.0.8.txt. This removes the public record of the vulnerability and its fix, which is important for security transparency and for downstream users to understand the risk.
findings.suggestion: Restore the CVE-2026-15920 advisory entries in both release notes files to maintain security transparency.
